Google SRE organization caps operational toil at 50% of each SRE's time, with the remaining 50% dedicated to engineering work that reduces future toil or adds service features.

SRE is fundamentally defined as applying software engineering principles to operations — hiring software engineers to run operations and creating systems to accomplish work that would otherwise be manual.
Error budgets resolve the structural conflict between development velocity and system reliability by quantifying acceptable unreliability.
SLI measures service behavior from the user perspective; SLO attaches SLIs to business value to communicate reliability across the organization.
Blameless postmortems are essential for incident learning — removing blame gives people confidence to escalate issues without fear, while blame culture drives incidents underground.
Postmortem triggers should be defined before incidents occur, including user-visible downtime, data loss, on-call intervention, resolution time thresholds, and monitoring failures.
Observability is the ability to understand a system's internal state by examining its outputs through three signal types: traces, metrics, and logs.
Proper instrumentation means developers don't need to add more instrumentation to troubleshoot issues because all necessary information is already available.
OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral instrumentation for traces, metrics, and logs, becoming the de facto standard for observability.
An Internal Developer Platform (IDP) is built by platform teams to create golden paths and enable developer self-service, lowering cognitive load without abstracting away context.
Platform Orchestrators have become the standard centerpiece of enterprise-grade IDPs, turning disjointed toolchains into cohesive platforms.
Successful platform engineering initiatives start small with a Minimum Viable Platform (MVP) approach and iterate quickly to continuously prove value to stakeholders.
Platform engineering maturity progresses through levels from initial ad-hoc capabilities to optimizing ecosystems where specialists extend platform capabilities.
Platform adoption typically starts slowly driven by platform builders, then accelerates as users pull adoption once platforms provide enough value.
Developer portals serve as the interface through which developers discover and access internal developer platform capabilities, but are not the platform itself.
Google's code review process maintains code quality and product quality through systematic examination by someone other than the author.
Heavyweight code review processes requiring multiple approvals before merging to trunk create a downward spiral where developers batch changes, making reviews even harder.
Synchronous code reviews (asking someone to review right then) are preferred over asynchronous reviews to minimize merge delays and conflicts.
Agent-generated pull requests require specialized review strategies to catch technical debt, hallucinated APIs, and over-engineered abstractions that AI tends to introduce.
Continuous Integration requires frequent integration to mainline, not just running CI tools on feature branches — the latter is semantic diffusion that causes confusion.
Feature toggles fall into distinct categories (Release, Experiment, Ops, Permission) that should be managed differently even if using the same technical machinery.
Ops Toggles control operational aspects of system behavior and should be reconfigured extremely quickly to allow operators to react to production issues.
Harness engineering — building specifications, quality checks, and workflow guidance that control AI agents — has emerged as a critical practice for human-AI collaboration in software development.

The difference between human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop is visible in response to unsatisfactory output: in-the-loop fixes the artifact directly; on-the-loop changes the harness that produces it.
Canary releases detect problems and regressions by rolling out changes to a subset of users, but should not be conflated with A/B testing which tests hypotheses.
The Strangler Fig pattern enables incremental legacy modernization by gradually replacing components while maintaining system operation.
Technical debt should be treated as a first-class backlog citizen with clear acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes such as faster build times or fewer flaky tests.
Agile teams treat resilience and maintainability as product features, scheduling refactors and practicing blameless incident response to reduce future cycle time.
DORA measures software delivery throughput through change lead time, deployment frequency, and failed deployment recovery time.
Version control ensures reproducibility and traceability, serving as a critical safety net as AI accelerates the velocity of change.
CI/CD pipelines automate the creation, testing, and deployment of applications, reducing errors in the deployment process by catching bugs early.
OWASP DevSecOps promotes shift-left security culture by integrating security testing (SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC scanning) early in the development pipeline.
Platform engineering success requires treating the platform as a product with dedicated product management, user research, and iteration based on feedback.
CNCF platform maturity model defines progression from basic capability provisioning to optimizing ecosystems with enabled specialist extensions.
Platform success metrics include user satisfaction (NPS), active users and retention, and developer productivity metrics from the SPACE framework.
Evolutionary architectures support modularity and well-defined boundaries that enable non-breaking changes, while inappropriate coupling inhibits evolution by propagating changes unpredictably.
Microservice teams favor open standards developed through live implementations over rigid corporate standards that lack recent programming experience.
Closing the data feedback loop from production enables continuous improvement by adapting models based on learnings from real production data.
Manual verification provides higher confidence that features behave as intended, complementing automated test coverage.
Pull requests add process to mainline pushes but can create significant friction for continuous integration when reviews take hours or days.
Pair programming creates continuous real-time code review as code is being written, producing a much faster feedback loop than asynchronous PR reviews.
Engineering work in SRE is novel, requires human judgment, produces permanent improvements, and enables the team to handle larger services with the same staffing.
